cohort: The study cohort consisted of febrile women who had blood cultures taken during their hospitalization for delivery, divided into BSI (n=85) and non-BSI (n=361) groups.
finding: Premature rupture of membranes (PROM), severe fever (>=38.9°C), and fever within 24 hours after delivery were identified as risk factors for peripartum BSI, which was associated with higher rates of maternal sepsis and lower neonatal Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections during labor were found to be more common in the BSI group.
